name: 90/90 Hip Stretch
description: Works internal and external hip rotation at once — the range most restricted by sitting.
instructions: Sit with the front leg bent 90 degrees in front and the back leg 90 degrees to the side.
Sit tall on both sit bones.
Lean forward over the front shin and hold.
Switch the legs and repeat.
tips: Sit on a cushion if you cannot stay upright
Move between sides rather than only holding
commonMistakes: Letting the spine round to reach further

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
description: One of the hardest anti-extension exercises — the core resists the spine arching.
instructions: Kneel and hold the wheel under your shoulders.
Brace hard and roll forward slowly.
Go only as far as you can keep the back flat.
Pull yourself back with the abs.
tips: Tuck the pelvis before you start rolling
Range comes from strength, not enthusiasm
commonMistakes: Letting the lower back sag into an arch
Rolling out further than you can return from

name: Air Bike
description: Fan-resistance cycling where the harder you work, the harder it pushes back.
instructions: Set the seat so the knee is slightly bent at full extension.
Push and pull the handles in time with the legs.
Work in intervals rather than long steady efforts.
Spin easy between hard efforts.
tips: Resistance scales with your effort — there is no easy gear
Short intervals are where this machine shines
commonMistakes: Going all-out on the first interval

name: Ankle Mobility Drill
description: Improves the ankle range that squat depth and running mechanics both depend on.
instructions: Stand facing a wall with one foot a hand-span away.
Keeping the heel down, drive the knee toward the wall.
Hold briefly, then release.
Move the foot back slightly as the range improves.
tips: The heel must stay flat — that is the whole drill
Track the knee over the second toe

name: Arnold Press
description: A press with a rotation, so the front and side delts both work through a longer range.
instructions: Start with dumbbells at chest height, palms facing you.
Rotate the palms outward as you press up.
Finish overhead with palms facing forward.
Reverse the rotation on the way down.
tips: Rotate smoothly through the whole press
Seated with back support if the lower back complains
commonMistakes: Rotating at the top instead of during the press
Going heavy before the pattern is smooth

name: Back Extension
description: Strengthens the spinal erectors and glutes — the muscles that keep a deadlift honest.
instructions: Set your hips on the pad with your feet secured.
Fold forward at the hips with a neutral spine.
Raise your torso until you are in a straight line.
Stop at straight — do not arch past it.
tips: Squeeze the glutes to finish the rep
Neutral neck: look at the floor, not forward
commonMistakes: Rounding the back on the way down

name: Band Face Pull
description: Rear-delt and upper-back work with a band — the most portable posture exercise there is.
instructions: Anchor a band at face height and hold both ends.
Pull the band toward your face, hands splitting apart.
Finish with your knuckles beside your ears.
Return slowly under tension.
tips: Externally rotate at the end of the pull
High reps — this is endurance work
commonMistakes: Pulling to the chest instead of the face
Letting the elbows drop below the shoulders

name: Barbell Curl
description: The heaviest biceps curl available, and the simplest to progress.
instructions: Stand holding the bar with an underhand shoulder-width grip.
Keep the elbows pinned to your sides.
Curl the bar to your chest.
Lower all the way to straight arms.
tips: Elbows do not travel forward
The lowering half builds as much as the lifting half
commonMistakes: Swinging the bar with the lower back
Cutting the bottom of the rep short

name: Barbell Overhead Press
description: The heaviest pressing most people can do overhead, and a genuine full-body brace.
instructions: Rack the bar at collarbone height, hands just outside the shoulders.
Brace the abs and squeeze the glutes.
Press the bar overhead, moving your head back slightly to clear it.
Lock out with the bar over your mid-foot.
tips: Ribs down — do not lean back to press
Finish with the biceps beside the ears
commonMistakes: Pressing around the head instead of over it

name: Barbell Row
description: The core horizontal pull — builds thickness through the whole upper back.
instructions: Hinge at the hips until your torso is about 45 degrees.
Hold the bar with an overhand grip, arms hanging.
Pull the bar to your lower ribs.
Lower under control without standing up.
tips: Lead with the elbows, not the hands
Keep the neck in line with the spine
commonMistakes: Standing up as the weight gets heavy

name: Battle Ropes
description: Intense conditioning with weighted ropes.
instructions: Hold ropes with knees slightly bent.
Whip ropes up and down quickly.
Maintain wave motion.
tips: Stay low
Move from shoulders

name: Bear Crawl
description: Quadrupedal crawling — a serious core and shoulder challenge disguised as cardio.
instructions: Start on hands and toes with the knees hovering just off the floor.
Move the opposite hand and foot together.
Keep the hips low and level.
Crawl forward, then reverse.
tips: Keep the knees an inch off the ground the whole time
Slow is harder than fast here
commonMistakes: Letting the hips rise into a downward dog
Moving the same-side hand and foot together

name: Bench Press
description: Standard upper body pressing movement for chest growth.
instructions: Lie on a bench with feet flat on floor.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width.
Lower the bar to mid-chest.
Press the bar back up to extension.
tips: Eyes under bar
Retract shoulder blades

name: Bicep Curls
description: Isolation exercise for the biceps.
instructions: Hold dumbbells with palms facing forward.
Curl weights toward shoulders.
Lower with control.
tips: Keep elbows pinned to sides
Full extension at bottom

name: Bird Dog
description: Teaches the trunk to stay still while the limbs move — the actual job of the core.
instructions: Start on hands and knees, spine neutral.
Extend one arm forward and the opposite leg back.
Hold briefly without letting the hips tilt.
Return and switch sides.
tips: Imagine balancing a glass of water on your lower back
Slow and deliberate beats fast reps
commonMistakes: Rotating the hips as the leg lifts
Lifting the limbs above shoulder or hip height

name: Box Jumps
description: Vertical power development.
instructions: Stand an arm's length from a stable box, feet hip-width apart.
Dip into a quarter squat and swing your arms back.
Drive up explosively and land softly on top of the box with both feet.
Stand tall, then step — do not jump — back down.
tips: Step down every rep; jumping down is where ankles get hurt
Land quietly with the knees tracking over the toes
commonMistakes: Choosing a box height that forces a deep tuck to clear

name: Bridge Pose
description: Strengthens the segments of the spine and legs.
instructions: Lie on back with knees bent.
Lift hips toward ceiling.
Clasp hands under back if possible.
tips: Chest to chin
Root through heels

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
description: A rear-foot-elevated single-leg squat — brutally effective for balancing left and right.
instructions: Place the top of one foot on a bench behind you.
Stand far enough forward that the front shin stays near vertical.
Lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor.
Drive up through the front heel.
tips: Front foot too close makes it a knee exercise
Lean forward slightly to bias the glute
commonMistakes: Standing too close to the bench

name: Burpees
description: A high-intensity full-body exercise that combines a squat, jump, and push-up.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Drop into a squat and place hands on floor.
Kick feet back into a plank.
Perform a push-up.
Jump feet back to hands.
Explode upwards into a jump.
tips: Breathe rhythmically
Land softly

name: Burpees with Push-Up
description: Enhanced burpee with extra chest work.
instructions: Drop into squat.
Jump to plank and do a full push-up.
Jump back and explode up.
tips: Consistent pace
Elbows in

name: Cable Crossover
description: Constant-tension chest work through a full arc, with no dead spot at the top.
instructions: Set both pulleys high and take a handle in each hand.
Step forward into a staggered stance.
Bring your hands down and together in front of your hips.
Return slowly against the resistance.
tips: Lean forward slightly from the hips
Cross the hands slightly for a stronger squeeze
commonMistakes: Using the whole body to swing the handles
Standing too far back and losing tension

name: Cable Crunch
description: A loadable crunch, so the abs can be progressed like any other muscle.
instructions: Kneel below a high pulley and hold the rope beside your head.
Hinge at the spine, not the hips.
Crunch down until the elbows approach the thighs.
Return slowly under tension.
tips: The hips stay fixed — only the spine flexes
Round the back deliberately; that is the movement
commonMistakes: Turning it into a hip hinge

name: Cable Row
description: Builds back thickness and strength.
instructions: Sit at the row machine with feet on platforms.
Pull the handle toward your abdomen.
Return to starting position with full reach.
tips: Keep back straight
Chest up

name: Calf Raises
description: Develops the gastrocnemius and soleus.
instructions: Stand on the edge of a step.
Raise your heels as high as possible.
Lower heels below the step level.
tips: Hold for a second at top
Full stretch at bottom

name: Calf Stretch
description: Strecthed the gastrocnemius.
instructions: Place hands on wall.
One foot back, heel on floor.
Lean in until stretch felt in calf.
tips: Back leg straight
Toe pointing forward

name: Cat-Cow Stretch
description: Spinal mobility flow.
instructions: Start on hands and knees, wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
Inhale and drop the belly, lifting the chest and tailbone into the cow position.
Exhale and round the spine, tucking the chin and tailbone into the cat position.
Move slowly between the two, one shape per breath.
tips: Let the breath set the pace, not the other way round
Move the whole spine, not just the lower back
commonMistakes: Bending only at the lumbar spine

name: Chest Dips
description: A leaning dip that loads the lower chest heavily through bodyweight.
instructions: Support yourself on parallel bars with arms locked.
Lean your torso forward about 30 degrees.
Lower until your upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Press back up, keeping the forward lean.
tips: Forward lean is what makes it a chest exercise
Stop the descent if the shoulder pinches

name: Chest Opener
description: Counteracts sitting with a chest stretch.
instructions: Clasp hands behind back.
Squeeze shoulder blades and lift arms.
Expand chest.
tips: Soft knees
Deep breaths

name: Child's Pose
description: Full back relaxation.
instructions: Kneel on the floor with the big toes together and knees apart.
Sit your hips back toward your heels.
Walk your hands forward and let your forehead rest on the mat.
Breathe into the back of the ribs and hold.
tips: Widen the knees if the belly gets in the way
A cushion under the hips helps if the heels are far away
commonMistakes: Lifting the hips instead of letting them settle

name: Chin-Ups
description: An underhand vertical pull — more biceps involvement than a pull-up, and usually a few more reps.
instructions: Hang from the bar with palms facing you, hands shoulder-width.
Pull until your chin clears the bar.
Lower under control to a full hang.
Keep the core braced so you do not swing.
tips: Drive the elbows down toward your ribs
A full hang at the bottom is part of the rep
commonMistakes: Kipping when unassisted reps run out

name: Close-Grip Bench Press
description: A bench press that shifts most of the work to the triceps while still letting you go heavy.
instructions: Lie on the bench and grip the bar shoulder-width apart.
Lower it to your lower chest with the elbows tucked.
Keep the elbows close to your sides throughout.
Press back to lockout.
tips: Shoulder-width, not narrower — the wrists suffer otherwise
Elbows tucked at about 45 degrees
commonMistakes: Gripping so narrow the wrists bend back

name: Cobra Pose
description: A gentle backbend that opens the chest and mobilises the thoracic spine.
instructions: Lie face down with the hands under the shoulders.
Press lightly and lift the chest.
Keep the elbows bent and close to the body.
Draw the shoulders down away from the ears.
tips: Lift with the back, not by pushing with the arms
Keep the hips and legs on the floor
commonMistakes: Straightening the arms and compressing the lower back

name: Concentration Curl
description: One arm, braced against the thigh, with maximum focus on the contraction.
instructions: Sit and brace your working elbow against the inside of your thigh.
Let the dumbbell hang.
Curl it toward your opposite shoulder.
Lower all the way down.
tips: Pause and squeeze hard at the top
Keep the torso still
commonMistakes: Rocking the body to move the weight
Choosing a weight that requires help

name: Corpse Pose
description: Complete stillness at the end of a session — this is where the nervous system down-shifts.
instructions: Lie flat on your back, arms a little away from the body.
Let the feet fall open naturally.
Close the eyes and release all effort.
Breathe slowly and stay for several minutes.
tips: Do not skip it — recovery is the point of the session
A cushion under the knees eases the lower back
commonMistakes: Continuing to hold tension in the jaw and shoulders

name: Couch Stretch
description: An intense hip-flexor and quad stretch for hips tightened by sitting.
instructions: Kneel with one shin against a wall, foot pointing up.
Bring the other foot forward into a lunge.
Squeeze the glute of the back leg and tuck the pelvis.
Rise upright until you feel a strong stretch, then hold.
tips: The pelvic tuck is what makes it work
Two minutes per side is a normal dose
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back to sit up taller
Holding the breath through the discomfort

name: Cycling
description: Steady-state cardio on a bike.
instructions: Adjust seat height so leg is nearly straight at bottom.
Pedal at a consistent RPM.
Vary resistance for intensity.
tips: Push and pull on pedals
Light grip on bars

name: Dead Bug
description: Safe core training.
instructions: Lie on your back with arms straight up and knees bent above the hips.
Press your lower back firmly into the floor and brace your abs.
Slowly lower one arm overhead and the opposite leg toward the floor.
Return to the start and repeat on the other side, keeping the back flat.
tips: Stop lowering the moment the lower back lifts
Exhale as the limbs extend
commonMistakes: Letting the lower back arch away from the floor
Moving fast enough that momentum takes over

name: Deadlift
description: The ultimate compound lift for total body strength.
instructions: Stand with feet mid-foot under the bar.
Bend at the hips and knees to grab the bar.
Keep your chest up and back flat.
Lift the bar by extending hips and knees.
tips: Pry bar against shins
Big breath at bottom

name: Decline Push-Up
description: A push-up with the feet elevated, shifting load toward the upper chest and shoulders.
instructions: Place your feet on a box or bench, hands under your shoulders.
Hold a straight line from heels to head.
Lower until your chest is just above the floor.
Press back up without letting the hips sag.
tips: The higher the feet, the harder it gets
Brace the abs as hard as on a plank

name: Devil Press
description: A burpee holding dumbbells, finishing with both weights swung overhead.
instructions: Place two dumbbells on the floor and drop into a burpee over them.
Complete a push-up with your hands on the handles.
Jump the feet in and hinge at the hips.
Swing both dumbbells overhead in one motion.
tips: Hinge to swing — do not curl the weights up
Start with very light dumbbells
commonMistakes: Rounding the back on the swing
Going too heavy and losing the hinge

name: Doorway Chest Stretch
description: Opens the chest and front shoulder — the direct counter to a rounded desk posture.
instructions: Place your forearm on a door frame, elbow at shoulder height.
Step forward with the same-side foot.
Rotate your chest away from the arm.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Try several elbow heights to reach different fibres
Gentle and sustained beats forceful
commonMistakes: Shrugging the shoulder toward the ear

name: Downward-Facing Dog
description: A foundational inversion that lengthens the hamstrings, calves and lats at once.
instructions: Start on hands and knees, hands slightly ahead of the shoulders.
Tuck the toes and lift the hips up and back.
Press the floor away and lengthen the spine.
Let the heels settle toward the floor.
tips: Bend the knees generously to get a long spine first
Spread the fingers and press through the knuckles
commonMistakes: Rounding the back to force the heels down
Collapsing the weight into the shoulders

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
description: Free-weight pressing that lets each side work independently and moves through a longer range than a barbell.
instructions: Lie on the bench holding a dumbbell in each hand at chest level.
Press both weights up until your arms are straight.
Lower under control until you feel a stretch across the chest.
Keep your feet planted and your lower back in a natural arch.
tips: Wrists stacked directly over elbows
Squeeze the chest at the top rather than locking hard
commonMistakes: Bouncing the weights off the chest

name: Dumbbell Chest Fly
description: An isolation movement that stretches and contracts the chest with the elbows nearly fixed.
instructions: Lie back holding dumbbells above your chest, palms facing each other.
Keep a soft bend in the elbows and open your arms wide.
Stop when you feel a stretch across the chest.
Bring the weights back together over your chest.
tips: Think of hugging a barrel
Lighter than you think — this is a stretch, not a press
commonMistakes: Bending and straightening the elbows (that is a press)
Going so deep the shoulder takes over

name: Dumbbell Row
description: One arm back strengthening.
instructions: Place one hand on bench.
Pull dumbbell to hip with other arm.
Keep back flat.
tips: Pull to hip, not armpit
Squeeze shoulder blade

name: Dumbbell Shrugs
description: Direct trap work — straight up, straight down, no rolling.
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Lift your shoulders straight toward your ears.
Hold the top for a beat.
Lower slowly to a full stretch.
tips: Pause at the top — that is where the work is
Keep the arms straight throughout

name: Dumbbell Side Bend
description: Direct oblique work through lateral flexion.
instructions: Stand holding a dumbbell in one hand at your side.
Bend sideways toward the weighted side.
Return by contracting the opposite oblique.
Complete all reps, then switch.
tips: Only one dumbbell — two cancels the resistance out
Keep the movement strictly side to side
commonMistakes: Twisting the torso as you bend

name: Elliptical Trainer
description: Low-impact cardio that keeps both feet in contact — useful when the joints need a break.
instructions: Step on and start with a light resistance.
Drive with the legs and push and pull with the arms.
Keep an upright posture.
Increase resistance rather than speed to work harder.
tips: Use the moving handles — it makes it a full-body effort
Do not lean on the console
commonMistakes: Gripping the fixed rails and sitting back

name: Face Pulls
description: Great for rear delts and posture.
instructions: Set cable to face height.
Pull rope toward your forehead, pulling ends apart.
Hold and return.
tips: Keep elbows high
Pause and squeeze

name: Flutter Kicks
description: Continuous lower-ab tension with a small, controlled range.
instructions: Lie on your back with the legs extended and hands under the hips.
Lift both heels a few inches off the floor.
Alternate small up-and-down kicks.
Keep the lower back pressed into the floor.
tips: Small, fast kicks beat big sloppy ones
Stop if the lower back lifts
commonMistakes: Kicking so high the abs disengage

name: Foam Roll Quads
description: Self-massage for the front of the thigh, useful before squatting or after a hard run.
instructions: Lie face down with the roller under one thigh.
Support your weight on your forearms.
Roll slowly from above the knee to the hip.
Pause on tender spots and breathe.
tips: Slow — a few centimetres per second
Pause rather than rolling back and forth quickly
commonMistakes: Racing through so fast nothing releases

name: Foam Roll Upper Back
description: Mobilises the thoracic spine and releases the muscles between the shoulder blades.
instructions: Lie back with the roller across your upper back.
Support your head with your hands.
Lift your hips and roll from mid-back to shoulders.
Pause and extend gently over tight spots.
tips: Stay above the bottom of the ribcage
Keep the abs braced so the lower back is protected
commonMistakes: Letting the head drop back unsupported

name: Front Raise
description: Isolates the front deltoid through a controlled arc.
instructions: Hold dumbbells in front of your thighs, palms facing you.
Raise one or both to shoulder height.
Keep a slight bend in the elbow.
Lower under control.
tips: Do not go above shoulder height
Alternate arms if the lower back complains
commonMistakes: Leaning back to start the lift
Going too heavy — the front delt is small

name: Front Squat
description: A squat with the bar in front, which forces an upright torso and loads the quads hard.
instructions: Rack the bar across the front of your shoulders, elbows high.
Keep the chest tall and the elbows up throughout.
Squat down until the thighs are at least parallel.
Drive up through mid-foot.
tips: Elbows dropping is what makes the bar roll forward
Wrist mobility matters more than grip strength here
commonMistakes: Rounding forward out of the bottom

name: Glute Bridges
description: Lying hip thrust movement.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, heels near your glutes.
Press through your heels and squeeze your glutes.
Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Pause at the top, then lower under control.
tips: Finish the rep with a hard glute squeeze, not a lower-back arch
Keep the ribs down as the hips rise
commonMistakes: Overextending the lower back at the top
Pushing through the toes instead of the heels

name: Goblet Squat
description: The best squat to learn on — the front-loaded weight self-corrects your posture.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell against your chest.
Stand with feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out.
Squat down between your knees, chest up.
Drive back up through the heels.
tips: Elbows can brush the inside of the knees at the bottom
The weight acts as a counterbalance — use it
commonMistakes: Letting the weight drift away from the chest

name: Hack Squat
description: A machine squat with a fixed path — heavy quad loading without balancing a bar.
instructions: Set your shoulders under the pads, feet mid-platform.
Release the safeties and lower under control.
Descend until the thighs are at least parallel.
Press back up without locking out hard.
tips: Feet higher on the platform spares the knees
Keep the lower back flat against the pad
commonMistakes: Letting the lower back round at the bottom
Bouncing out of the bottom position

name: Hammer Curl
description: A neutral-grip curl that builds the brachialis and forearm — this is what adds arm thickness.
instructions: Hold dumbbells at your sides, palms facing each other.
Curl one or both up, keeping the palms facing in.
Squeeze at the top.
Lower slowly.
tips: Keep the wrist locked neutral
Often allows more weight than a supinated curl
commonMistakes: Leaning back to finish the lift

name: Hamstring Stretch
description: Classic hamstring stretch.
instructions: Sit on the floor with one leg extended and the other bent inward.
Sit tall and lengthen your spine first.
Hinge forward from the hips over the straight leg.
Hold where you feel a stretch, breathe, then switch sides.
tips: Fold from the hips, not by rounding the back
A small bend in the knee is fine and often better
commonMistakes: Rounding the spine to reach the toes
Bouncing at the end of the range

name: Hanging Leg Raise
description: A demanding lower-ab movement that also builds grip and shoulder stability.
instructions: Hang from a bar with the arms straight.
Brace the abs and stop any swinging.
Raise your legs until they are at least parallel to the floor.
Lower them slowly.
tips: Curl the pelvis up at the top — that is the ab work
Bend the knees to make it easier
commonMistakes: Lifting with the hip flexors only

name: High Knees
description: Running in place with high knee drive.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Drive one knee up toward your chest, at least to hip height.
Switch legs quickly, staying on the balls of your feet.
Pump the arms in time with the legs.
tips: Stay tall — do not lean back as you tire
Quick, light contacts beat big slow ones
commonMistakes: Letting the knees drop below hip height

name: Hip Flexor Stretch
description: Opens up tight hip flexors.
instructions: Kneel on one knee.
Push hips forward slightly.
Keep torso tall.
tips: Squeeze glute of back leg
Don't over-arch

name: Hip Thrust
description: The best exercise for glute isolation.
instructions: Sit on floor with back against bench, bar over hips.
Drive through heels to lift hips.
Squeeze glutes at top and lower.
tips: Chin tucked
Don't hyper-extend back

name: Hollow Hold
description: Gymnastics foundational core hold.
instructions: Lie on back.
Lift feet and shoulders 6 inches off floor.
Press lower back into ground.
tips: Force lower back down
Breathe through core

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
description: Pressing on an incline to bias the upper chest, the area most people under-train.
instructions: Set the bench to about 30 degrees.
Start with the dumbbells at upper-chest level.
Press up and slightly back over your collarbones.
Lower slowly to the stretch position.
tips: 30 degrees is enough — steeper turns it into a shoulder press
Drive your shoulder blades into the bench
commonMistakes: Letting the weights drift toward the face

name: Incline Press
description: Targets the upper chest fibers.
instructions: Lie on an incline bench at 30-45 degrees.
Lower the bar to your upper chest.
Press back to extension.
tips: Don't let elbows flare 90 deg
Solid foot placement

name: Incline Walk
description: Walking uphill — most of the cardio benefit of running with a fraction of the joint load.
instructions: Set the incline to 8 to 12 percent.
Walk at a pace that feels sustainable.
Stand tall and let the arms swing.
Reduce the incline gradually to finish.
tips: Do not hold the rails — it removes most of the work
Excellent option on rest days from lifting
commonMistakes: Choosing a speed so high you have to jog

name: Inverted Row
description: A bodyweight horizontal pull you can scale by changing your body angle — the best on-ramp to pull-ups.
instructions: Set a bar at hip height and hang underneath it.
Keep your body in a straight line, heels on the floor.
Pull your chest to the bar.
Lower until the arms are straight.
tips: Walk the feet forward to make it harder
Squeeze the glutes to hold the line
commonMistakes: Pulling with the arms and leaving the back out

name: Jump Jacks
description: Traditional calisthenics.
instructions: Stand upright with your feet together and arms at your sides.
Jump your feet out wide while sweeping your arms overhead.
Jump your feet back together and bring the arms down.
Keep a steady rhythm and land softly through the mid-foot.
tips: Soft knees on every landing
Step out instead of jumping for a low-impact version
commonMistakes: Only half-raising the arms as fatigue sets in

name: Jump Rope
description: High-burn cardio that builds coordination.
instructions: Hold rope ends at sides.
Jump as rope passes under feet.
Maintain a steady rhythm.
tips: Jump on balls of feet
Use wrists to turn rope

name: Jump Squat
description: An explosive squat that builds power and raises the heart rate immediately.
instructions: Start in a quarter-squat position.
Drive up and jump as high as you can.
Land softly through the mid-foot.
Absorb the landing into the next rep.
tips: Land quietly — noise means you are absorbing badly
Quality over quantity; stop when the landings deteriorate
commonMistakes: Letting the knees collapse inward on landing

name: Kettlebell Clean and Press
description: A hip-driven clean into an overhead press — power, strength and conditioning together.
instructions: Hike the kettlebell back between your legs.
Snap the hips to bring it to the rack position.
Press it overhead once it settles.
Lower to the rack, then back to the swing.
tips: The clean is a hip movement, not an arm curl
Keep the wrist straight in the rack position
commonMistakes: Letting the bell crash onto the forearm
Pressing before the bell is stable

name: Kettlebell Swings
description: Power-focused hip hinge movement.
instructions: Hinge at hips to grab KB.
Snap hips forward to swing KB to chest height.
Hinge back as KB falls.
tips: Drive with hips, not arms
Core tight at top

name: Lat Pulldown
description: Simulates a pull-up with adjustable weight.
instructions: Sit at the machine and grab the wide bar.
Pull the bar down to your upper chest.
Release back up slowly.
tips: Squeeze shoulder blades
Slight lean back

name: Lateral Raise
description: The one movement that builds shoulder width — pressing alone will not do it.
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Raise the weights out to shoulder height.
Lead with the elbows, wrists neutral.
Lower slowly, resisting the whole way.
tips: Light weight, strict form — ego costs you the side delt
Stop at shoulder height
commonMistakes: Swinging the weights up with the hips
Shrugging so the traps take the load

name: Leg Curl
description: The only common movement that trains the hamstring at the knee rather than the hip.
instructions: Lie or sit with the pad against your lower calves.
Curl your heels toward your glutes.
Squeeze at the fully bent position.
Lower slowly under control.
tips: Keep the hips down on a lying machine
Pair with Romanian deadlifts for full hamstring coverage
commonMistakes: Lifting the hips off the pad

name: Leg Extension
description: Isolates the quadriceps with no balance or lower-back demand at all.
instructions: Sit with the pad resting on your lower shins.
Extend your knees until the legs are straight.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly to the start.
tips: Squeeze the quad at lockout
Slow negatives matter more than heavy weight
commonMistakes: Swinging the weight up with momentum
Letting the plates crash down between reps

name: Leg Press
description: Machine-based leg training.
instructions: Sit in the machine with feet shoulder-width apart.
Lower the platform toward your chest.
Push it back up without locking knees.
tips: Keep back flat on seat
Controlled descent

name: Lunges
description: Unilateral leg exercise for balance and strength.
instructions: Step forward with one leg.
Lower hips until both knees are at 90 degrees.
Push back to start.
tips: Keep torso upright
Don't let front knee pass toes

name: Lying Leg Raise
description: The floor version of the hanging leg raise — accessible and just as effective early on.
instructions: Lie on your back with your hands under your hips.
Keep the legs straight and the lower back pressed down.
Raise the legs to vertical.
Lower slowly, stopping before the back arches.
tips: Stop lowering the moment the back lifts off
Bend the knees to shorten the lever
commonMistakes: Letting the lower back arch away from the floor

name: Mountain Climbers
description: A dynamic core exercise that also provides a cardio boost.
instructions: Start in a plank position.
Alternately bring your knees toward your chest quickly.
Keep your movements smooth and controlled.
tips: Hands under shoulders
Back flat

name: Neck Release
description: Releases the neck and upper traps — for tension headaches and phone posture.
instructions: Sit or stand tall with the shoulders down.
Tilt one ear toward the shoulder.
Rest a hand lightly on your head for gentle weight.
Hold, breathe, then switch sides.
tips: The weight of the hand alone is enough
Keep the opposite shoulder pressed down
commonMistakes: Rolling the neck in full circles

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
description: One of the most effective hamstring-injury preventers there is, and one of the hardest.
instructions: Kneel with your ankles anchored under something solid.
Keep the hips straight and the body in one line.
Lower forward as slowly as you can.
Catch yourself with your hands, then push back up.
tips: Even a small controlled range is worthwhile
Use a band or a partner to assist at first
commonMistakes: Bending at the hips to make it easier

name: Outdoor Run
description: Running outside — varied terrain, real wind resistance, and better adherence for most people.
instructions: Start easy for the first five minutes.
Settle into a rhythm you could sustain for double the distance.
Keep the cadence quick and the steps light.
Walk the last few minutes to cool down.
tips: Cadence around 170 to 180 steps per minute reduces impact
Run by effort, not pace, on hills
commonMistakes: Ignoring a niggle until it becomes an injury

name: Overhead Tricep Extension
description: The overhead position stretches the long head of the triceps, which pushdowns barely reach.
instructions: Hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands.
Keep the elbows pointing forward, close to your head.
Lower the weight behind your head.
Extend back to overhead.
tips: Elbows stay narrow throughout
Brace the abs so the ribs do not flare
commonMistakes: Elbows splaying out to the sides
Arching the lower back to help

name: Pallof Press
description: An anti-rotation press — you resist a twist rather than creating one.
instructions: Stand side-on to a cable or band at chest height.
Hold the handle at your sternum with both hands.
Press it straight out and resist the pull toward the anchor.
Return to the chest.
tips: The further you step from the anchor, the harder it gets
Squeeze the glutes to lock the hips
commonMistakes: Letting the torso rotate toward the anchor
Holding the breath through the press

name: Pigeon Pose
description: A deep hip-opener for the glutes and rotators — the antidote to long hours sitting.
instructions: From all fours, bring one knee forward behind that wrist.
Slide the other leg straight back.
Square the hips toward the floor.
Fold forward over the front shin and breathe.
tips: Support the hip with a cushion if it does not reach
Back the intensity off if the knee complains
commonMistakes: Forcing depth through a painful knee

name: Pike Push-Up
description: The bodyweight route to an overhead press — no equipment needed.
instructions: Start in a push-up position, then walk your feet in to pike the hips high.
Lower the crown of your head toward the floor.
Press back up until the arms lock.
Keep the hips high the whole time.
tips: The higher the hips, the more vertical the press
Elevate the feet to progress
commonMistakes: Letting the hips drop into a push-up
Craning the neck instead of bending the arms

name: Plank
description: An isometric core exercise that builds stability and endurance.
instructions: Hold a push-up position but rest on your forearms.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core and hold.
tips: Look at floor
Squeeze glutes

name: Plank with Rotation
description: Core stability and rotational power.
instructions: Start in side plank.
Rotate torso and reach under.
Return to side plank.
tips: Hips high
Eyes on hand

name: Plate Squeeze Press
description: Press two plates together and push them out — pure inner-chest tension with almost no equipment.
instructions: Press your palms hard together at chest height.
Keeping the pressure on, push your hands straight out.
Pause when the arms are extended.
Draw them back to your chest, still squeezing.
tips: Squeeze harder than you push
Great as a finisher or a warm-up
commonMistakes: Rushing — this is a tension exercise

name: Preacher Curl
description: The pad removes momentum entirely, so the biceps has nowhere to hide.
instructions: Rest the back of your upper arms on the pad.
Start with the arms almost straight.
Curl the weight up to your shoulders.
Lower until just short of full lockout.
tips: Control the bottom — it is the vulnerable position
Do not let the elbows slide off the pad
commonMistakes: Dropping the weight at the bottom
Lifting the elbows off the pad to cheat

name: Pull-Ups
description: Bodyweight exercise for a wider back.
instructions: Grab the pull-up bar with palms facing away.
Pull your body up until your chin is over the bar.
Lower yourself back down with control.
tips: Pull elbows to floor
Keep core engaged

name: Push-Ups
description: A classic upper body exercise that builds strength in the chest and arms.
instructions: Start in a plank position.
Lower your body until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Push back up to the starting position.
tips: Core tight
Elbows at 45 degrees

name: Quad Stretch
description: Stretches the quadriceps.
instructions: Stand on one leg.
Grab other ankle and pull to glute.
Push hips forward.
tips: Keep knees together
Hold for 30s

name: Rear Delt Fly
description: Hits the rear deltoid and upper back — the fix for shoulders rounded forward by desk work.
instructions: Hinge forward until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor.
Let the dumbbells hang beneath your chest.
Raise them out to the sides in a wide arc.
Lower slowly.
tips: Thumbs slightly down as you lift
Very light — this muscle is small and stubborn

name: Resistance Band Curl
description: Biceps work with the resistance rising as you curl — hardest exactly where you are strongest.
instructions: Stand on the middle of the band and hold an end in each hand.
Keep the elbows at your sides.
Curl your hands toward your shoulders.
Lower slowly against the band.
tips: Step wider on the band for more resistance
Fight the band on the way down
commonMistakes: Letting the band snap the arms back down

name: Resistance Band Tricep Extension
description: A portable pushdown — anchor the band high and press down.
instructions: Anchor the band above head height.
Hold the end with elbows tucked at your sides.
Extend the arms down until straight.
Return under control.
tips: Keep constant tension — never let it go slack
Step further away to increase resistance
commonMistakes: Elbows drifting away from the body
Using body weight to push down

name: Romanian Deadlift
description: Excellent for developing the posterior chain.
instructions: Hold bar at hip height.
Hinge at hips, keeping bar close to legs.
Lower until you feel a big stretch in hamstrings.
Drive hips forward to return.
tips: Keep back flat
Knees slightly bent

name: Rowing Machine
description: Low-impact, full-body cardiovascular training.
instructions: Drive with legs first.
Pivot hips and pull handle to chest.
Return in reverse order.
tips: 60% legs, 20% core, 20% arms
Smooth stroke

name: Russian Twist
description: Torso rotation strength.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and heels lightly touching down.
Lean your torso back to about 45 degrees and brace your abs.
Rotate your shoulders and hands to one side.
Rotate smoothly to the other side, keeping the chest lifted.
tips: Rotate the ribcage, not just the arms
Lift the heels to make it harder
commonMistakes: Swinging the hands while the torso stays still
Letting the back round as you tire

name: Seated Cable Row
description: A supported horizontal pull — easy to learn and easy to load safely.
instructions: Sit with your feet on the platform and a slight knee bend.
Reach forward to take the handle, chest up.
Pull to your navel, driving the elbows back.
Let the handle travel forward until you feel a stretch.
tips: Squeeze the shoulder blades at the end of the pull
Keep the torso still — it should not rock
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso back and forth

name: Seated Calf Raise
description: A bent-knee calf raise, which targets the soleus underneath the main calf muscle.
instructions: Sit with the pad across your thighs and the balls of your feet on the platform.
Let the heels drop for a full stretch.
Press up onto the toes as high as possible.
Lower slowly.
tips: Pause at both ends of the range
High reps — the calf is built for endurance
commonMistakes: Skipping the stretch at the bottom

name: Seated Forward Fold
description: A calming hamstring and lower-back stretch held for longer durations.
instructions: Sit with the legs extended straight ahead.
Lengthen the spine upward first.
Hinge at the hips and fold forward.
Hold and let the breath deepen the position.
tips: Bend the knees slightly if the back rounds
Fold from the hips, not the waist
commonMistakes: Yanking on the feet to force depth
Rounding the spine to reach further

name: Shoulder Press
description: Overhead press for strong shoulders.
instructions: Sit or stand with dumbbells at shoulder height.
Press dumbbells overhead until arms are extended.
Lower back to starting position.
tips: Don't arch back
Look straight ahead

name: Shoulder Stretch
description: Cross body shoulder stretch.
instructions: Stand or sit tall with your shoulders relaxed and down.
Bring one arm straight across your chest at shoulder height.
Use the opposite hand on the upper arm to draw it closer.
Hold, breathe, then repeat on the other side.
tips: Keep the stretched shoulder pressed down, not shrugged
Pull on the upper arm, never on the elbow joint
commonMistakes: Shrugging the shoulder toward the ear
Rotating the torso to increase the stretch

name: Shuttle Run
description: Short sprints with hard changes of direction — conditioning plus deceleration work.
instructions: Mark two points about 10 to 20 metres apart.
Sprint to the far marker and touch the line.
Turn sharply and sprint back.
Rest, then repeat.
tips: Drop the hips to decelerate before turning
The turn is where the training effect is
commonMistakes: Rounding the turn instead of stopping and driving
Sprinting through with no rest between efforts

name: Side Plank
description: Builds oblique strength.
instructions: Lie on side supported by forearm.
Lift hips until body straight.
Hold.
tips: Shoulder over elbow
Feet stacked

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
description: One side at a time, so the stronger side cannot compensate for the weaker.
instructions: Place one knee and hand on a bench, the other foot on the floor.
Let the dumbbell hang straight down.
Row it to your hip, elbow close to the body.
Lower all the way until the shoulder stretches.
tips: Pull toward the hip, not the shoulder
Keep the shoulders square to the floor
commonMistakes: Twisting the torso to lift more
Cutting the bottom of the range short

name: Skullcrusher
description: A lying triceps extension that loads the long head through a deep stretch.
instructions: Lie on a bench holding the weight above your chest.
Keeping the upper arms still, bend at the elbows.
Lower the weight toward your forehead.
Extend back to the start.
tips: Only the forearms move
Angle the arms slightly back to keep tension at the top

name: Sled Push
description: Total body conditioning push.
instructions: Grip sled handles and lean in.
Drive with legs to push sled forward.
Maintain a 45 degree body angle.
tips: Small steps
Eyes down

name: Sprint Intervals
description: Alternating max effort with recovery.
instructions: Sprint at 90% effort for 30s.
Walk/Jog for 60s.
Repeat.
tips: High knee drive
Pump arms

name: Squats
description: A fundamental lower body exercise that targets the quads, hamstrings, and glutes.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Lower your hips as if sitting in a chair.
Keep your chest up and back straight.
Return to the starting position.
tips: Weight on heels
Knees track over toes

name: Stair Climber
description: Intense lower body cardio.
instructions: Climb steps at a steady pace.
Avoid leaning heavily on side rails.
Keep posture upright.
tips: Full steps
Engage glutes

name: Step-Up
description: A single-leg push that carries directly into stairs, hills and everyday life.
instructions: Stand facing a box at about knee height.
Place one whole foot on the box.
Drive through that heel to stand up on top.
Lower under control — do not drop.
tips: All the work comes from the top leg
Control the way down; that is half the exercise
commonMistakes: Using a box so high the hip has to hike

name: Stiff Leg Deadlift
description: High hamstring activation variant.
instructions: Hinge at hips with nearly straight legs.
Lower bar beyond shins.
Return to vertical.
tips: Go to your limit of flex
Don't lock knees binary

name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
description: Isolates the lats with the arms locked, so the biceps cannot take over.
instructions: Stand facing a high pulley, holding the bar with straight arms.
Hinge slightly at the hips, chest up.
Pull the bar down to your thighs in an arc.
Return slowly overhead until the lats stretch.
tips: Elbows stay almost straight the whole time
Feel it in the armpit, not the triceps
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows into a pushdown
Using body weight to drive the bar down

name: Sumo Deadlift
description: A wide-stance deadlift that shortens the range and shares the load with the hips and quads.
instructions: Take a wide stance with the toes turned out.
Grip the bar inside your knees.
Drop the hips, chest up, and push the floor away.
Lock out by driving the hips forward.
tips: Open the knees out over the toes
The bar stays in contact with the legs
commonMistakes: Letting the bar drift away from the shins

name: Sun Salutation
description: A flowing sequence that warms the whole body and links movement to breath.
instructions: Stand tall, then sweep the arms overhead as you inhale.
Fold forward as you exhale.
Step or jump back to a plank, lower, then lift into an upward dog.
Press to a downward dog, then walk forward and rise.
tips: One movement per breath
Repeat five rounds as a complete warm-up
commonMistakes: Letting the hips sag in plank

name: Swimming
description: Full-body, zero-impact conditioning that also demands real shoulder mobility.
instructions: Warm up with two easy lengths.
Swim intervals with short rests at the wall.
Exhale steadily underwater and breathe bilaterally.
Finish with easy lengths to loosen off.
tips: Breathing rhythm matters more than arm speed
Push off the wall with a streamlined body
commonMistakes: Holding the breath instead of exhaling underwater
Lifting the head to breathe rather than rotating

name: Tabata Squats
description: 20s max effort squats, 10s rest for 8 rounds.
instructions: Perform as many squats as possible in 20s.
Rest for 10s.
Repeat 8 times total.
tips: Explosive speed
Keep form safe despite fatigue

name: Thoracic Rotation
description: Restores rotation to the upper back — the mobility most desk workers have lost.
instructions: Start on all fours and place one hand behind your head.
Rotate that elbow down beneath your body.
Then open it up toward the ceiling, following with your eyes.
Move slowly through the full range.
tips: Rotate from the ribcage, not the lower back
Follow the elbow with your gaze
commonMistakes: Moving fast and bouncing at the end range

name: Thruster
description: A front squat into an overhead press — one of the most metabolically demanding movements there is.
instructions: Hold the weight at shoulder height.
Squat to at least parallel.
Drive up explosively out of the bottom.
Use that momentum to press the weight overhead.
tips: One continuous movement, not two separate lifts
Pace yourself — this spikes the heart rate fast
commonMistakes: Pausing between the squat and the press
Pressing before the legs have finished driving

name: Toe Touch Crunch
description: A straightforward upper-ab crunch with the legs held vertical.
instructions: Lie on your back with the legs pointed straight up.
Reach both hands toward your toes.
Lift the shoulder blades off the floor.
Lower with control.
tips: Lead with the chest, not the chin
Exhale hard at the top
commonMistakes: Bouncing off the floor between reps

name: Treadmill Run
description: Steady-state running with pace and incline you control precisely.
instructions: Start with a five-minute walk to warm up.
Build to a pace you can just hold a conversation at.
Keep your stride relaxed and land under your hips.
Finish with a five-minute cool-down walk.
tips: A 1% incline better matches outdoor running
Do not hold the handrails
commonMistakes: Starting at goal pace with no warm-up
Over-striding out in front of the body

name: Tree Pose
description: Balance based focus pose.
instructions: Stand tall and shift your weight onto one foot.
Place the sole of the other foot on the inner calf or inner thigh — never the knee.
Press the foot and leg into each other and find your balance.
Bring the hands to the chest or overhead, and hold while breathing steadily.
tips: Fix your eyes on a still point ahead
Toes of the lifted foot can rest on the floor while you build balance
commonMistakes: Resting the foot directly against the knee joint
Letting the standing hip push out to the side

name: Triangle Pose
description: A standing pose that stretches the hamstrings and side body while building leg stability.
instructions: Stand with the feet wide, front foot turned out.
Reach forward over the front leg, then tip sideways.
Rest the lower hand on your shin or the floor.
Extend the top arm toward the ceiling.
tips: Think long side body rather than deep reach
Stack the shoulders vertically
commonMistakes: Collapsing the chest toward the floor

name: Tricep Dips
description: Dip station arm training.
instructions: Support weight on bars.
Lower body by bending elbows.
Push back to straight arms.
tips: Keep torso upright for triceps
Control the descent

name: Tricep Kickback
description: Peak triceps contraction at full extension, with almost no joint stress.
instructions: Hinge forward with the upper arm parallel to your torso.
Start with the elbow bent at 90 degrees.
Extend the forearm back until the arm is straight.
Return under control.
tips: Squeeze for a full second at lockout
Light weight — the leverage is brutal
commonMistakes: The upper arm dropping during the rep

name: Tricep Pushdown
description: The most joint-friendly way to load the triceps directly.
instructions: Stand at a high pulley holding the bar or rope.
Pin the elbows to your sides.
Push down until the arms are straight.
Let the bar rise until the forearms are parallel to the floor.
tips: Elbows stay glued to the ribs
Spread a rope apart at the bottom for a harder squeeze
commonMistakes: Leaning over the bar to press with body weight

name: Tuck Jump
description: A maximal vertical jump pulling the knees to the chest.
instructions: Start standing with the feet hip-width.
Dip quickly and jump as high as possible.
Pull both knees toward your chest at the peak.
Land softly and reset before the next rep.
tips: Reset between reps rather than chaining them sloppily
High impact — build up gradually
commonMistakes: Tucking the heels instead of lifting the knees
Continuing once the landings get heavy

name: Upright Row
description: A vertical pull for delts and traps. Use a wider grip to keep the shoulder happy.
instructions: Hold the bar in front of your thighs, hands shoulder-width or wider.
Pull it up along your body, leading with the elbows.
Stop when the upper arms reach shoulder height.
Lower under control.
tips: Wider grip is far kinder to the shoulder joint
Stop at shoulder height, never higher
commonMistakes: Narrow grip plus a high pull — a classic impingement recipe
Jerking the bar with the legs

name: V-Ups
description: Advanced core compression movement.
instructions: Lie on back.
Simultaneously lift legs and torso to touch toes.
Balance on tailbone at top.
tips: Keep legs straight
Slow descent

name: Walking Lunge
description: Lunges that travel, adding a balance and conditioning demand to the strength work.
instructions: Step forward into a lunge until both knees are at 90 degrees.
Drive through the front heel to stand.
Bring the back foot through into the next lunge.
Keep the torso upright throughout.
tips: Longer steps hit the glutes, shorter steps the quads
Look ahead, not down
commonMistakes: Front knee sliding far past the toes
Letting the back knee crash into the floor

name: Wall Sit
description: An isometric hold that builds quad endurance with zero equipment and zero impact.
instructions: Stand with your back flat against a wall.
Slide down until your knees are at 90 degrees.
Keep your knees over your ankles and your back flat.
Hold for time.
tips: Weight through the heels, not the toes
Breathe steadily — do not hold your breath
commonMistakes: Sliding above 90 degrees as it gets hard
Resting the hands on the thighs

name: Warrior 1
description: Builds focus, power, and stability.
instructions: Step one foot forward into a lunge.
Turn back foot 45 degrees.
Reach arms to ceiling.
tips: Square hips to front
Deep breath

name: Warrior 2
description: Strengthens legs and builds focus.
instructions: Step your feet wide apart and turn the front foot out 90 degrees.
Line up the front heel with the arch of the back foot.
Bend the front knee until it is stacked over the ankle.
Extend the arms out at shoulder height and gaze over the front hand.
tips: Front knee tracks over the second toe
Keep the torso stacked over the hips, not leaning forward
commonMistakes: Letting the front knee collapse inward
Leaning the torso out over the front leg
